svg.title: POST /auth/resend-otp — detailed implementation workflow
svg.desc: Level 2 · real functions, middleware and models · badges map to the 8 stages in auth-api-04-resend-otp-overview.svg
svg.text: Level 2 · real functions, middleware and models · badges map to the 8 stages in auth-api-04-resend-otp-overview.svg
Independent of the server's own timer

g.text: Same bucket as all 5 other auth routes.
Same lookup shape as every other auth
429 with the exact seconds remaining if
Failure here throws to the catch-all 500.
Password reset re-sends never call this route — ForgotPassword.js's own "Resend" action calls POST
/auth/forgot-password again instead (see AUTH-API-05), confirmed by tracing every caller of this endpoint.
from client 120 s vs. server 120 s
A page refresh resets OTPForm's visible
countdown to 120 s even if the server's own
cooldown has nearly elapsed — the button can
appear disabled longer than actually required.
Counts against the same 20-per-15-min IP budget
as signup, login and every other OTP/reset route.

svg.text: Heavy arrows are region hand-offs; the cyan one is the HTTP response. Light arrows are steps inside a region. Absent mechanisms — a refresh token, a server session, frontend JWT decoding — are named in a note, never drawn as implemented steps.
A fresh OTP fully replaces the previous one — the old code stops working the moment this succeeds, not just after its original expiry.
